Dexamethasone, a synthetic glucocorticoid, is implicated in the pathogenesis of Ankylosing Spondylitis (AS) through its anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects. The evidence suggests that Dexamethasone may act as a repurposed therapeutic agent for AS, as it is linked to Psoriatic Arthritis and Crohn Disease, both of which are associated with AS through their inflammatory pathways. The indirect pathways involve the use of biologics such as Etanercept and Infliximab, which are tumor necrosis factor (TNF) inhibitors, and Certolizumab Pegol, a monoclonal antibody targeting TNF-alpha. These biologics are known to modulate the immune response and reduce inflammation, which are key mechanisms in AS.

The integration of these pathways highlights the potential of Dexamethasone to influence the inflammatory cascade in AS, particularly through its ability to suppress immune-mediated damage. The scores from the paths indicate a moderate level of confidence in this relationship, suggesting that Dexamethasone may exert a therapeutic effect on AS by targeting inflammatory processes, though further mechanistic validation is required to confirm its direct role in the disease. The evidence supports a plausible mechanism of action, but the exact nature of the interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
